blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Typed e-mail address written to the log platform on a failed lookup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail to greet by name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (e.g. `no customer for this e-mail`), or carry it in a field the error handler never logs. The `errorHandler` registered at src/routes.ts:21 logs `err.message` (`logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })` in src/server.ts), and src/logger.ts ships every line to the log platform: every lookup with no match puts the typed e-mail address — a customer's or a mistyped third party's — into the logs, with no retention rule of its own (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 5(1)(e), Art. 32). The same holds, to a lesser degree, for the customer id at src/support.ts:32.
findings.title: Typed e-mail address written to the log platform on a failed lookup

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — the proposal says the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to": the customer id and name. Drop `email`, `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` from `chatWidgetSettings` (and stop selecting them in `customerById` if nothing else uses them). As written, every page load of `/chat/settings` (src/routes.ts:13-19) hands the full record to the browser and to the Helply widget script, i.e. to a third-party processor, beyond the purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c), Art. 25, Art. 28).
findings.title: Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail to greet by name

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: State which fields an agent needs to recognise the customer and return only those from `/support/customers/lookup`; the proposal's purpose is that agents stop asking customers "who they are", which the id, name and e-mail may already serve. Birth date and postal address are kept only if the team confirms a need (e.g. identity verification) — a question for the controller (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)).
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date, address and phone with no stated need

findings.evidence: /** What the Helply chat widget is started with, for the signed-in customer. */
findings.recommendation: Ask the team to confirm that Helply is covered by a processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28), listed in the record of processing (Art. 30), and where it stores the data (Chapter V if outside the EEA), and how erasure requests reach the copy Helply keeps. The plan only says "the chat vendor receives who is chatting".
findings.title: Helply not identified as a processor, nor its data location
